projects.title: Hatag — Direct Browser-to-Browser File Transfer
projects.desc:
Hatag — Direct Browser-to-Browser File Transfer

A privacy-focused browser-based file transfer application that sends files directly between devices over an encrypted WebRTC connection — with QR/code pairing, offline support, transfer verification, and no account or cloud storage.

Overview

Hatag was built as a lightweight alternative to traditional file-sharing services. Instead of uploading files to a cloud server and having the receiver download them, Hatag establishes a direct connection between two browsers and transfers the files directly between the devices.

The application is completely web-based and can be hosted as a static site on GitHub Pages. GitHub only delivers the application itself — the files being transferred never pass through GitHub Pages or another storage server.

Hatag uses WebRTC DataChannels for peer-to-peer file transfer, with QR codes and short pairing codes used to exchange the connection information between devices. Once connected, files travel directly between the sender and receiver through an encrypted DTLS connection.

The application is also designed to work without internet access after its initial load. A service worker caches the application shell, allowing devices on the same local network to continue using Hatag even when the internet is unavailable.

Key Features

📱 Direct Device-to-Device Transfer — Files are transferred directly between the two browsers using a WebRTC DataChannel instead of being uploaded to cloud storage.

🔐 Encrypted Peer-to-Peer Connection — WebRTC provides an encrypted DTLS connection between the devices, keeping the file transfer direct and private.

📷 QR Code Pairing — The sender generates a QR code containing connection information that the receiver can scan using a phone camera or the built-in scanner.

🔢 6-Digit Pairing Codes — Each transfer session also generates a short six-digit code, providing an alternative to QR scanning when cameras are unavailable.

🔄 Two-Way Connection Handshake — Hatag uses a sender code and receiver reply code to complete the WebRTC connection without requiring a signaling server.

📂 File & Folder Selection — Users can drag files into the application or select individual files and folders for transfer.

📊 Large File Support — The transfer system uses chunked DataChannel transmission with configurable buffer limits to prevent excessive memory usage during large transfers.

✅ SHA-256 Verification — Files can be verified after transfer using SHA-256 hashing to ensure the received data matches the original.

📈 Live Transfer Progress — The interface displays transfer progress, speed, transferred data, file progress, and overall transfer status.

❌ Cancel & Decline Controls — Transfers can be cancelled while in progress, while receivers can review an incoming transfer and decline it before accepting.

📱 Cross-Platform Browser Support — Designed to work between PC, Android, iPhone, and other modern browsers supporting WebRTC.

🌐 Offline-Ready — Once the application has been loaded and cached, Hatag can operate without internet access. Devices only need a local network connection for direct transfers.

📡 LAN-First Architecture — Same-network transfers do not require public servers or internet connectivity. Optional public STUN support can be enabled for devices located on different networks.

☁️ No Cloud Storage — Files are never uploaded to Hatag, GitHub Pages, or another cloud storage service.

👤 No Account Required — Users can start transferring files immediately without creating an account or providing personal information.

🧹 Automatic Session Expiration — Pairing sessions expire after a configurable period, with the default session lifetime set to five minutes.

💾 Transfer History — Local history allows users to keep track of previous transfers without requiring a remote database.

⚙️ Optional Signaling Relay — A small optional relay can automate the exchange of the WebRTC reply information when users do not want to perform the second QR/code exchange. The relay handles connection information only and never receives the transferred files.

📦 Progressive Web App — Hatag includes a web manifest and service worker, allowing it to behave like an installable application on supported devices.

projects.title: E-Commerce & Custom Ordering Website
projects.desc:
Joev's Engraving & Printing Services — E-Commerce & Custom Ordering Website

A modern responsive e-commerce website for a custom engraving and printing business, featuring a product catalog, product search, shopping cart, online ordering and quotation flow, customer messaging, and business location integration.

Overview

The Joev's Engraving website was built from the ground up to bring a traditional engraving and printing business into a modern online storefront.

The website combines a business landing page with a custom product catalog, allowing customers to browse awards and personalized products, search for specific items, add products to a shopping cart, and proceed to an online ordering or quotation workflow.

Unlike a conventional e-commerce store, the website is designed around custom-made products where materials, dimensions, finishes, quantities, and personalization requirements can vary between orders.

The platform also connects customers directly with the business through Facebook, phone, Viber, email, and Google Maps, making it possible to discover products, request an order, communicate with the business, and locate the physical workshop from one website.

Key Features

🛍️ Online Product Catalog — Browse a wide range of custom products including glass, acrylic, crystal, wood, resin, medals, diploma holders, frames, brass plates, mugs, gift sets, and sale items.

🔍 Product Search — Built-in product search allows customers to quickly find products directly from the website.

🛒 Shopping Cart — Customers can add products to a cart, review selected items, and proceed to the ordering process. The cart also provides an empty-state experience with a direct link back to the product catalog.

📋 Online Ordering & Quotations — A dedicated Order Now / Get Quote flow allows customers to begin an order for customized products where final requirements may need confirmation from the business.

🎨 Custom Product Support — Product categories are designed around customizable materials, dimensions, finishes, engraving, printing, and presentation requirements. For example, plaques and bases can have different sizes and finishes, while medals support custom dimensions.

📱 Responsive Web Design — The interface is designed to work across desktop and mobile devices, with responsive navigation and dedicated mobile controls.

⚡ Business Service Highlights — The homepage prominently communicates rush-order availability, free layout services, Metro Manila delivery, and premium-quality production.

💬 Customer Communication — Direct contact options include phone, Viber, email, and Facebook messaging, allowing customers to discuss custom requirements and orders.

📍 Workshop Location — Google Maps integration provides customers with access to the physical workshop location and navigation.

🏆 Business-Focused Landing Page — The homepage combines product discovery with business information, services, contact details, and calls-to-action such as Order Now and View Products.

🧩 Custom E-Commerce Experience — Instead of treating the website as a simple static company page, the platform integrates catalog browsing, search, cart functionality, and custom-order workflows into a single experience.

projects.title: Math x Time Adventure
projects.desc:
MathxTime Adventure — Think Fast. Solve Smart

A magical math adventure game for Android where players solve math problems, write answers by hand, explore fantasy worlds, defeat bosses, collect rewards, and build confidence in addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

Overview

MathxTime Adventure turns math practice into an interactive fantasy adventure — combining educational gameplay with handwriting recognition, world exploration, boss battles, progression systems, achievements, statistics, and collectible Magic Pens.

Players can explore multiple magical worlds filled with math challenges, earn stars and rewards, unlock new levels, defeat powerful bosses, and progress toward becoming a Math Master. The game supports multiple ways to practice mathematics, from structured Adventure Mode to fast-paced competitive challenges.

Built from the ground up as a native Android application using Kotlin, MVVM, Jetpack Navigation, ViewBinding, Room, DataStore, Firebase, and ML Kit Digital Ink for handwriting recognition.

Designed for families and learners with no advertisements, no required account, email, or real name. Core game progress remains stored locally on the device, while online functionality is optional.

Key Features

🗺️ Magical World Adventure — Explore fantasy worlds containing progressively challenging math levels, unique environments, rewards, and boss battles. Adventure progression automatically controls which levels and worlds become available.

✍️ Handwriting Math Input — Write answers directly on the screen using natural handwriting instead of typing. ML Kit Digital Ink recognizes handwritten numbers through the custom HandwritingCanvasView and HandwritingManager.

🎮 Multiple Game Modes — Play math in different ways:

  • Adventure Mode — Explore worlds and defeat bosses.

  • Endless Mode — Continue solving questions and see how far you can go.

  • Survival Mode — Solve problems while protecting your remaining lives.

  • Time Attack — Solve as quickly as possible against the clock.

  • Practice Mode — Practice specific math skills at your own pace.

  • 100 Challenge Mode — Complete 100 questions as quickly and accurately as possible.

🪄 Magic Pen Collection — Collect, purchase, equip, and master Magic Pens with different rarities, unlock conditions, visual effects, sounds, and cosmetic properties. The Magic Pen system integrates with the existing pen-color system while providing a larger collection and progression framework.

✨ Magical Writing Effects — Equipped Magic Pens can produce custom trails, particles, sounds, and correct-answer effects directly on the handwriting canvas. Current effects include Wood Pencil, Nature, Inferno, Frost, Thunder, Bubble, Galaxy, and Rainbow.

📖 Player Spellbook — A personal journal containing the player's avatar, Magic Pen collection, cosmetics, themes, titles, and achievements, allowing players to track and customize their journey.

🏆 Achievements & Player Progression — Earn achievements, XP, coins, gems, titles, cosmetics, login bonuses, and other rewards while progressing through the game.

📊 Statistics & Insights — Game performance is recorded across supported modes, with aggregate statistics and post-game coaching insights generated through the statistics and teacher insight systems.

🔥 Magic Pen Mastery — Gain mastery XP by correctly answering questions while using a Magic Pen. Progress through Novice, Adept, Expert, and Master tiers, with mastery affecting visual effects only and providing no gameplay advantage.

🎃 Seasonal Events — Participate in recurring seasonal events featuring special Event Pens and limited-time content. Current events include Halloween, Christmas, Summer, and Anniversary.

🌎 Optional Global Leaderboard — Players can optionally participate in competitive gameplay and compare their performance through a global leaderboard powered by Firebase and anonymous authentication.

🔒 Family-Friendly & Privacy Focused — No advertisements, no required account, email, or real name. Core game data is stored locally, while online features are optional.

💎 Optional Premium Content — The game includes a monetization architecture for Magic Crystals, Crystal Pens, Premium Pens, bundles, and other cosmetic content. Premium items are designed to remain cosmetic and provide no gameplay advantage. Real Google Play Billing integration is currently planned but not yet integrated.

projects.title: ThermoLink
projects.desc:
ThermoLink — Wireless IR Temperature Scanner A professional-grade contactless temperature screening app for Android, powered by ESP8266/ESP32 — with live thermal imaging, guided face detection, a real-time web dashboard, and full scan history export.

Overview

ThermoLink is the full Android successor to the original Wireless IR Temperature Scanner — a maker project first published on Instructables and Hackster.io that used a simple serial-over-Bluetooth link to a desktop app. That original worked well for one sensor and one use case, but had no screen feedback, no history, and no thermal imaging.

ThermoLink rebuilds the whole idea from the ground up: native Android, Wi-Fi TCP, support for 10 different IR sensors including thermal arrays, on-device face detection, a live web dashboard accessible from any browser on the same network, and XLSX export — while keeping the same ESP8266 hardware most makers already have on the bench.

Built for kiosk deployments, clinics, schools, and any high-throughput contactless screening environment where precision and auditability both matter.

Key Features

🌡️ Guided Scan Flow — The scan screen walks a subject through a defined sequence: camera activates, ML Kit detects a face, on-screen prompts guide positioning above the eyebrows, then temperature is captured on tap. Auto-resets for the next person in 3 seconds. No accidental triggers, no continuous background scanning.

📸 Manual Capture Mode — Three dedicated buttons (Take Photo, Capture Temp, Save Scan) let operators stage photo and temperature independently and commit both in a single tap — useful when auto-capture stalls or full manual control is preferred.

🔆 Live Thermal Heatmap — Array sensors (AMG8833, MLX90640, MLX90621, Omron D6T) stream a live iron-palette heatmap directly on the scan screen and web dashboard in real time, giving visual confirmation of scan positioning and hot-spot detection.

🖥️ Live Web Dashboard — While connected, ThermoLink hosts an HTTP server on the phone accessible from any browser on the same Wi-Fi. The dashboard shows live temperature and label, live heatmap, room conditions (temperature, heat index, humidity), a 50-scan trend chart, label distribution chart, full scan history with photos, browser voice readout, and one-click CSV export.

📊 10 Supported Sensors — Covers single-point IR sensors (MLX90614, MLX90615, MLX90632, TMP007) and thermal arrays (AMG8833, Panasonic Grid-EYE, MLX90640 at 32×24, MLX90621, Omron D6T-44L, Omron D6T-8L). All connect over I²C with the same 3-wire ESP wiring.

📶 Wi-Fi TCP + Bluetooth — Primary connection is Wi-Fi TCP (recommended) with auto-reconnect to the last used device on launch. Bluetooth Classic via HC-05/HC-06 is also supported for environments without a local network.

📁 Scan History & Export — Every scan is saved locally with timestamp, temperature, Normal/Elevated/Fever label, optional photo, and device name. One-tap XLSX export from the History screen; CSV export from the web dashboard.

🔒 Fully On-Device & Private — No data leaves the local network. Face detection runs entirely offline via bundled ML Kit. No analytics, no accounts, no cloud.

⚙️ Deep Configurability — Per-sensor calibration offset, custom fever/elevated thresholds, auto-scan trigger, voice guidance and voice readout, beep/vibrate/flash alerts on fever detection, background foreground service, weather overlay, and configurable scan delay.

projects.title: Remote Control Cloner
projects.desc:
Remote Control Cloner A hobbyist Android app for cloning and transmitting IR remote codes — capture any remote using Arduino or ESP hardware over Bluetooth, then fire codes directly from your phone's IR blaster.

Overview

Remote Control Cloner started the same way most projects do — a broken remote, a pile of spare ESP32 boards, and the question: why can't my phone just do this?

Most phones with IR blasters ship with a generic remote app that either requires picking from a fixed brand list or relies on an internet-connected database that may or may not have your device. If your remote is old, obscure, or just not in anyone's database, you're stuck.

This app takes a different approach: you capture the IR codes directly from your physical remote using a VS1838B IR receiver wired to an Arduino or ESP board, transmitted to the phone over Bluetooth. No guessing, no database lookup — you're cloning the exact signals your device already responds to.

Once captured, codes are stored locally on the phone. Any button on any remote — TV, aircon, sound system, projector, videoke machine — becomes a button in the app. From there you can transmit via the phone's built-in IR blaster, customise button labels and colours, share remotes with other users, or browse the community library for remotes others have already built.

The project also grew a community side — a shared Firebase Firestore library where users can publish and browse remotes with no account needed, and a live online database pulling from Flipper-IRDB and irdb covering thousands of devices across NEC, Samsung, Sony, and RC5 protocols.

Key Features

📡 IR Capture via Bluetooth — Pairs with an Arduino Uno, ESP32, or ESP8266 + VS1838B IR receiver over Bluetooth Classic. Captures raw IR timings in microseconds and stores them per button. Works with any IR remote regardless of brand or protocol.

📲 Transmit from Phone — Fires captured IR codes through the phone's built-in IR blaster. Supports tap-once and hold-to-repeat for volume, channel, and navigation buttons. Compatible with most Xiaomi, Samsung, and OPPO devices with hardware IR blasters.

🎨 Fully Customisable Buttons — Each button has configurable label, colour, shape (rounded, circle, pill, square), and size (S/M/L). Drag-to-reorder within the grid. Button types include Standard, Power, D-Pad, Number, and Touchpad layouts.

🌍 Community Library — Powered by Firebase Firestore. Users publish remotes directly from the save dialog — no account, no approval process. Stars let the community flag remotes that actually work. Appears for all users within seconds of publishing.

🗄️ Online IR Database — Browses Flipper-IRDB and irdb live via jsDelivr CDN — nothing bundled in the APK. Organised by category (TV, Receiver, DVD, Projector, Audio, Satellite). Tap a remote to download and use instantly. Star to save to My Remotes.

✏️ Manual IR Code Editor — Every button exposes its raw IR data in Pronto Hex format. Paste codes from LIRC, IrScrutinizer, or any IR code database. Also accepts raw microsecond timings with optional explicit carrier frequency.

📦 Export / Import — Remotes export as human-readable .json files shareable via WhatsApp, Drive, Gmail, or any file app. Import accepts single remotes or bulk files containing multiple remotes.

🔌 External IR Dongle Support — For phones without a hardware IR blaster, audio-based 3.5mm and USB-C IR dongles are supported via the audio output pipeline. Requires phone DAC with ≥ 96 kHz sample rate.

🔧 Three Hardware Targets — Firmware provided for ESP32 (built-in Bluetooth, 3 wires only), ESP8266 + HC-05/HC-06, and Arduino Uno/Nano + HC-05/HC-06. All three use IRremote v4.7.1 with a consistent serial capture protocol.

projects.title: Scanora — QR & Barcode Scanner · Maker
projects.desc:
Scanora — QR & Barcode Scanner · Maker A fully offline Android app for scanning and generating QR codes and barcodes, built with Kotlin and Jetpack — no internet required, no data collected, no compromises.

Overview

Scanora is the successor to QR Scanner Maker plus Ultra, an earlier Android scanner project that was discontinued after its last release in January 2024. That version was a functional 3-in-1 scanner built in HTML/WebView, but it had a significant limitation: QR code generation required an internet connection, and the architecture had hit a ceiling.

 Scanora is the full ground-up rewrite — native Kotlin, proper Jetpack components, and a completely offline pipeline for both scanning and generation. Everything that was a workaround in the old app became a design requirement in the new one.

Most scanner apps either require internet access, quietly harvest your scan history, or bury basic features behind ads. Scanora is built as a clean alternative: everything runs on-device using bundled ML Kit, nothing leaves your phone, and the interface stays out of the way so you can scan or generate codes and get back to what you were doing. It supports a wide range of formats on both the scanning and generation sides, with enough customization to make generated codes actually useful.

Key Features

📷 Live Camera Scanner — Continuously scans QR codes and all major barcode formats using CameraX and bundled ML Kit (fully offline). Includes pinch-to-zoom, a seekbar zoom control, flashlight toggle with optional auto-flash in low light, and beep/vibrate feedback on successful reads.

🖼️ Gallery Import — Scan a code from any image already on the device, useful when someone sends you a screenshot or a QR code via chat.

🔁 Batch Mode — Keeps scanning continuously without stopping between reads, useful for rapid multi-item workflows.

🔲 QR Code Generator — Creates QR codes for Text, URL, Email, Phone, SMS, vCard Contacts, Wi-Fi credentials, Geo locations, and Calendar events. Supports custom foreground and background colors, output size, error correction level, embedded logo/icon, and optional label text below the code. Fully offline — no internet required, unlike the previous version.

📊 Barcode Generator — Generates Code 128, Code 39, EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, ITF, Codabar, PDF417, Aztec, Data Matrix, and more via ZXing core.

🎯 Smart Result Screen — Detected content type drives contextual action buttons automatically: Open URL, Call, Send SMS, Add Contact, Connect Wi-Fi, Open Map, or Add to Calendar — no manual parsing by the user.

🗂️ Local History — All scans and generated codes are saved to a Room (SQLite) database, filterable by Scanned/Generated, searchable by content, and configurable for limits from 25 entries up to unlimited. Swipe-to-delete with undo.

🔒 100% Offline & Private — No INTERNET permission is declared. All processing, history, and preferences stay on-device and are never transmitted anywhere.

projects.title: Barcode Generator/Designer
projects.desc:
Barcode Generator/Designer
A desktop barcode label designer and printer built with C# and Windows Forms, purpose-built for retail and inventory workflows that require precise, print-ready barcode labels generated directly from spreadsheet data.

Overview

This project solves a practical pain point in warehouse and retail operations — manually typing product data to generate individual barcodes is slow and error-prone. Barcode Generator/Designer lets staff load an entire product roster from an Excel or CSV file, map spreadsheet columns to label fields in a guided UI, preview the result at high resolution, and print batches in one pass. Every element on the label — from barcode position to font size to fill style — is precisely tunable without touching code.

Key Features

🔲 Multi-Format Barcode Generation — Supports Code 128 (auto, subset B/C), Code 39, EAN-13, and UPC-A. EAN-13 and UPC-A check digits are auto-computed from 12/11-digit input, and ZXing renders the symbology at a fixed 300 DPI with nearest-neighbor scaling and binary thresholding for clean, scannable output.

📄 Excel & CSV Batch Import — A guided import form loads .xlsx, .xls, .csv, and .tsv files via ClosedXML. A column-mapping wizard lets users assign spreadsheet columns to label fields (barcode value, description, price, right/left labels, and up to 10 custom text fields) and saves mappings per preset, eliminating re-mapping on repeat runs.

🎨 Fully Composable Label Layout — Every text element (store name, product description, price, rotated right-side label, left label, and 10 custom fields) has independently configurable X/Y position, font family, font size, bold toggle, word wrap, and black-fill inversion — all adjustable via numeric controls with a live preview that re-renders on each change.

🖨️ Print & Print Preview — Batch printing queues all imported rows and cycles through them automatically, with configurable print offset to compensate for printer margin drift. A dedicated print-preview mode renders each label at full resolution before committing to paper.

💾 Preset System with GitHub Sync — Label layouts are saved as named presets in a local database_presets.json file. A SyncService class handles upload and download to a GitHub repository via the Contents API, automatically resolving create vs. update using file SHA, keeping the label database portable and version-controlled across machines.

📐 DPI-Normalized Rendering — The label bitmap is pinned to 120 DPI internally so text renders pixel-identically across machines regardless of Windows display scaling, preventing layout overflow on high-DPI displays.

projects.title: Aero — U-Robot Link Universal Robot Controller
projects.desc:
Aero — U-Robot Link

A universal Android robot controller app published on the Google Play Store, designed to eliminate the need to build a custom remote-control app for every new robotics project. One app. Every platform.

Overview

Aero was built to solve a recurring problem in the maker and robotics community — every new project meant reinventing the same controller UI from scratch. Aero replaces that by providing a single, polished Android app that speaks a simple serial protocol over Bluetooth, BLE, or WiFi, and automatically translates it into the correct binary protocol when connecting to LEGO MINDSTORMS hardware.

Whether you're driving an Arduino car, monitoring IoT sensors, or controlling a LEGO EV3 robot — Aero handles it all without writing a single line of controller code.

Key Features

📡 Multi-Protocol Connectivity     Supports Bluetooth Classic (HC-05/HC-06), BLE (HM-10, ESP32), and WiFi TCP (ESP8266, ESP32) — all from the same device connection screen. Includes auto-reconnect on startup for frequently used devices.

🤖 LEGO MINDSTORMS Support (NXT & EV3)     Connects natively to LEGO NXT and EV3 bricks using the official LEGO Direct Commands protocol over Bluetooth — no custom firmware, no ev3dev, no leJOS required. Motor port mapping, directional inversion, brake-on-stop, deadband, and max power are all configurable from within the app.

🎮 10 Control Modes     Includes a fully customizable button grid, dual joystick with differential drive math, tilt control via accelerometer, gamepad support for PS4/PS5/Xbox controllers, RGB color picker, serial terminal, countdown timer with auto-send, voice control via Google Speech Recognition, a live IP camera viewer (MJPEG), and a full IoT sensor dashboard.

📊 IoT Sensor Dashboard     Parses SENSOR:key:value messages from any connected device and auto-generates live widgets — gauge, chart, bar, LED indicator, compass, and more — with color-coding, threshold alerts, drag-to-reposition layout, and profile saving. Supports up to 500 readings per sensor in memory.

🌐 Built-in Web Dashboard     Runs a local WebSocket server on port 8080 that lets any browser on the same WiFi view live sensor data, sparkline charts, history tables, and CSV exports — no cloud, no subscription, fully offline.

📱 Live Camera Stream     Streams MJPEG video from ESP32-CAM or any compatible IP camera directly in the app, operating independently from the robot control connection.

🧩 Saved Profiles & Dark Mode     Multiple named profiles per device for switching between control layouts (e.g. "Drive Mode", "Arm Mode", "IoT Mode"). Full light/dark theme support for outdoor and low-light use.

projects.title: QR Attendance System
projects.desc:
QR-SMS Attendance System

A desktop attendance management application built with C# and Windows Forms, designed to streamline student check-in/check-out using QR code scanning and automated SMS notifications to guardians.

Overview

This project addresses a common pain point in school administration — manual attendance tracking is slow, error-prone, and leaves parents out of the loop. The QR-SMS Attendance System replaces that process with a real-time, camera-based solution that logs attendance and immediately notifies a student's guardian via SMS the moment they arrive or are dismissed.

Key Features

📷 QR Code Scanning     Uses the device's webcam to continuously scan for student QR codes in real time, with a live camera feed, bounding-box overlay on successful scans, and intelligent decode throttling to keep CPU usage low.

📋 Student Database Integration     Loads a student roster directly from an Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx), automatically mapping columns for name, LRN, phone number, address, year level, section, track/strand, guardian, and more. No manual re-entry required.

📲 Automated SMS via Webhook     On a successful scan, the app builds a personalized SMS message and dispatches it to a connected Android device via a webhook endpoint. Messages are fully customizable with template placeholders and include a 5-second cooldown per student to prevent duplicate sends.

⏱ On-Time / Late Detection     Compares the scan timestamp against a configurable scheduled time and automatically stamps each log entry as On Time, Late, or Dismissed for OUT scans.

📁 CSV Attendance Logging     Every scan is written to a persistent attendance.csv file with full student details, timestamp, and IN/OUT status — ready for reporting or further processing.

🔲 QR Code Generator     Built-in tool to generate and save QR codes from any text input, making it easy to produce student ID QR codes directly within the same application.

projects.title: Spongebot
projects.desc:
Spongebot

A SpongeBob SquarePants-themed Arduino robot built as a personal gift, controlled wirelessly via a custom Android app over Bluetooth. A passion project that combines embedded hardware, custom industrial design, and mobile app development into one character-accurate, fully functional robot.

Overview

Spongebot started as a personal project — a one-of-a-kind SpongeBob robot built and gifted to someone special. Rather than using an off-the-shelf controller, a dedicated Android app was designed and built specifically for it, giving the robot a polished user experience that matched its personality. The result is a fully self-contained system: power it on, open the app, and it connects automatically.

Key Features

📱 Dedicated Android App     A custom-built Android application (.apk) designed exclusively for Spongebot. The app auto-connects to the robot via Bluetooth on launch — no manual pairing steps needed after the first setup.

🔵 Bluetooth Wireless Control     Communicates over Bluetooth Classic using an HC-05 module. A built-in LED indicator on the robot provides clear connection feedback — blinking red means not connected, steady red means connected and ready.

🎨 Custom Physical Design     The robot body was designed and built to resemble SpongeBob, with a custom layout crafted to match the character's proportions and look. Design files are included in the repository under the sponge layout folder.

⚡ Arduino-Powered Firmware     The robot's onboard logic runs on Arduino firmware written in C/C++, handling Bluetooth command parsing and motor/actuator control. Circuit schematics and Fritzing diagrams are included for full reproducibility.

Tech Stack

CategoryDetails
MicrocontrollerArduino
FirmwareC / C++ (Arduino IDE)
WirelessBluetooth Classic (HC-05)
Mobile AppAndroid (Custom APK)
Circuit DesignFritzing
Physical DesignCustom layout / enclosure

projects.title: QR Scanner Maker Plus Ultra
projects.desc:
QR Scanner Maker Plus Ultra

A 3-in-1 Android QR and barcode utility app published on the Google Play Store, combining real-time camera scanning, photo-based QR reading, and QR code generation into a single lightweight tool.

Overview

Most QR apps do one thing — scan. QR Scanner Maker Plus Ultra does three. Whether you need to scan a code in real time, decode a QR from an existing photo in your gallery, or generate a brand-new QR code from any text or URL, this app handles all of it from a single interface. Two of the three features work fully offline, making it reliable even without a data connection.

Key Features

📷 Real-Time QR & Barcode Scanner     Uses the device camera to instantly scan and decode QR codes and barcodes in real time. Works entirely offline — no internet connection required.

🖼️ Scan QR from Photos     Reads and decodes QR codes directly from images stored in the device gallery. Useful for codes that have already been photographed or saved as screenshots. Also works offline.

✨ QR Code Generator     Generates a QR code from any text, link, or data input. Allows users to instantly create shareable QR codes for their own content.

📦 3 Releases on GitHub     Actively maintained with 3 published releases, with the latest version (v1.0.2) released in January 2024.

projects.title: Portable RetroPie Mini Arcade
projects.desc:
Portable RetroPie Mini Arcade

A handheld retro gaming console built from scratch using a Raspberry Pi 4, a 7-inch touchscreen, and a custom-designed enclosure — capable of emulating dozens of classic game consoles in a portable, self-contained form factor.

Overview

This project takes the open-source RetroPie platform and packages it into a compact, purpose-built arcade cabinet you can carry anywhere. Rather than using a generic case, the enclosure was designed from scratch with precise dimensions, fabricated in acrylic, and also released as a fully printable 3D STL file on Thingiverse — so anyone can replicate the build. The result is a portable gaming machine that plays classic titles from NES, SNES, PS1, Game Boy, and dozens of other platforms, all on a 7-inch touchscreen with built-in audio.

Key Features

🖥️ 7-Inch Capacitive Touchscreen Display     Powered by the Waveshare 7-inch HDMI LCD (1024×600 resolution) with capacitive touch support. Connected to the Raspberry Pi 4 via Micro HDMI, delivering a crisp, responsive display for both gaming and navigation through the RetroPie menu.

🎮 Raspberry Pi 4 Brain     Built on the Raspberry Pi 4 (2GB), offering more than enough processing power to run emulators for older consoles smoothly. Supports both wired USB joystick controllers and Bluetooth gamepads for flexible control options.

🔊 Built-in Audio     An 8Ω 5W speaker mounted at the back of the LCD screen provides onboard audio — no external speaker or headphones required.

🔋 Fully Portable     Powered entirely by a powerbank, making the unit wireless and play-anywhere without needing a wall outlet. The Raspberry Pi and the display each draw from the same bank, keeping the setup clean and cable-minimal.

📦 Custom-Designed Enclosure     The housing was designed with exact dimensions (275mm × 158mm front/back, 132mm depth) and built using acrylic panels and angle brackets. A 3D-printable STL version of the full enclosure was also published on Thingiverse for the community to reproduce.

🕹️ RetroPie Software Stack     Runs RetroPie on a 64GB SD card, pre-loaded with a full multi-console image (Dual Screen Raspberry Pi4 RetroPie "CRT BLAST" build from ArcadePunks). Supports ROMs from a wide range of classic platforms, configured with the correct emulators and BIOS files out of the box.

⚙️ Optional Desktop PC Mode     With an optional Raspbian OS setup, the same unit can boot into a full Raspberry Pi desktop environment — functioning as a portable mini-PC for browsing, documents, and more when not gaming.

projects.title: Wireless IR Temperature Scanner
projects.desc:
Wireless IR Temperature Scanner

A contactless Bluetooth temperature scanner built with Arduino and an MLX90614 infrared sensor, designed to allow safe, distance-based body temperature readings viewed in real time through a custom Android app. Published on Hackster.io and the Google Play Store.

Overview

This project was built as a practical response to the need for non-contact fever screening — a situation where a person monitoring temperatures at a building entrance has to stand close to each individual, raising their own risk of exposure. The Wireless IR Temperature Scanner solves this by placing the sensor device near the entrance while the operator monitors readings from up to 9 meters away via Bluetooth on their phone.

"Touch Less and Do More."

Key Features

🌡️ Non-Contact Infrared Sensing     Uses the MLX90614 infrared thermometer sensor, which reads both ambient (room) and object (body) temperatures without any physical contact. Accuracy is ±0.02°C over an object temperature range of -70°C to 382.2°C — well within the precision needed for human fever screening.

📡 Wireless Bluetooth Transmission     Temperature data is transmitted wirelessly via an HC-06 Bluetooth module with a range of up to 9 meters, allowing the monitoring operator to maintain a safe distance from the person being screened.

📱 Dedicated Android App (Google Play Store)     A companion app — Wireless IR Temperature Scanner Plus ULTRA — was built and published to the Google Play Store. It pairs with the device over Bluetooth and displays live ambient and object temperature readings with color-coded fever thresholds: Normal (34.8°C – 37.3°C), High (37.4°C – 38°C), and Fever (38.1°C+).

🔋 Portable & Self-Contained     Powered by a standard 9V battery with an on/off rocker switch. The circuit was hand-soldered onto a universal PCB with female pin headers for modular assembly, making it easy to modify or repair.

📖 Fully Documented & Published     Complete build documentation — including schematics, wiring diagrams, firmware, and step-by-step instructions — was published on both Hackster.io and Instructables, accumulating over 11,000 views on Hackster alone.

projects.title: WiFi Default Password Plus ULTRA
projects.desc:
WiFi Default Password Plus ULTRA

An Android utility app published on the Google Play Store that generates the default WiFi password for common Philippine ISP routers — particularly PLDT — based on the network's SSID or MAC address. A practical tool for users who've forgotten their router's factory password and need to recover it without a reset.

Overview

Many home routers in the Philippines ship with passwords algorithmically derived from their SSID or MAC address. This project reverse-engineers those generation algorithms and wraps them into a clean, easy-to-use Android app. Instead of manually performing hex conversions or multiplications by hand, users simply input their network details and the app instantly calculates the likely default password. The app covers 8 distinct router SSID types across PLDT Fibr, PLDT Home DSL, and HomeBro networks.

Key Features

🔐 Multi-Algorithm Password Generation     Each supported router type uses a different algorithm, all implemented within the app: hex complement conversion (for PLDTFIBR and PLDTHOMEFIBR variants), MAC address suffix extraction (for PLDTHOMEDSL and HomeBro), and hexadecimal-to-decimal multiplication (for numeric and alphanumeric DSL SSIDs).

📶 Supports 8 SSID Types     Covers the most common PLDT router variants used across the Philippines, including PLDTFIBR_xxxxxx, PLDTHOMEFIBRxxxxx, PLDTHOMEDSL, PLDTmyDSLPAL, PLDmyDSLBiz, PLDTHOMEDSLxxxxx (numeric and alphanumeric), and HomeBro_Ultera.

📱 Published on Google Play Store     Available as a free download with 2 released versions (v1.3 latest), accumulating 9 stars and 3 forks on GitHub — demonstrating real community adoption and interest.

⚡ Instant, Offline Generation     All password generation logic runs entirely on-device with no internet connection required. Users input their SSID or MAC address and get the computed default password immediately.

Supported Algorithms

SSID FormatAlgorithm
PLDTFIBR_xxxxxxLast 6 of SSID → hex complement → prepend wlan
PLDTHOMEFIBRxxxxxLast 6 of SSID → hex complement → prepend PLDTWIFI
PLDTHOMEDSL / PLDTmyDSLPALLast 5 of MAC address → prepend PLDTWIFI
HomeBro_UlteraLast 6 of MAC address → prepend HomeBro_
PLDTHOMEDSLxxxxx (numeric)Last 5 digits × 3 → prepend PLDTWIFI
PLDTHOMEDSLxxxxx (alphanumeric)Last 5 (hex → decimal) × 3 → prepend PLDTWIFI

Tech Stack

PlatformAndroid
DistributionGoogle Play Store
LogicSSID/MAC-based password generation algorithms
LanguageJava (Android SDK)
